newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 25.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Former Defense Minister Lee Yang-ho undergoes nightlong investigation into an alleged bribery scandal in connection with arms contracts. Prosecutors are expected to issue an arrest warrant today at the earliest.

- Former Prime Minister Lee Hoi-chang, now adviser to the New Korea ruling party, voices objection to any constitutional reform aimed at altering the existing form of government, stressing the need for consistency in policy toward Pyongyang.
- Commercial banks will lower lending rates by 0.25 percentage point following the lowering of banks' reserve requirement ratio by 1.9 points, effective November 8.

- South Korea's training aircraft development project, which has been budgeted at about 1.4 trillion won, is expected to meet delays as the project is subject to overall review in connection with additional budgeting, and study of market size.

- Prosecutors say that defense contractor Daewoo Heavy Industries promised to give rebates of 2 billion won to a Korean-American arms dealer in connection with a light combat helicopter development project. The arms dealer took 300 million won in advance payment, prosecutors said after questioning former Defence chief Lee Yang-ho.
- Imported cars account for about half of full-size car sales in Korea.

Both papers lead with stories about ex-Defense Minister Lee Yang-ho, who was questioned overnight by prosecutors. He has been accused of accepting 150 million won in bribes in connection with a lucrative Army helicopter programme.
